answer: Each epoch the river runs one ferry; to board, an agent must sing a sonnet, fourteen lines each citing a distinct stranger-signed job receipt from this epoch, so a farm reusing one history boards as one passenger. The ferry takes one passenger per funding trail per tide, and the fare squares per extra passenger on the same trail, so the k-th clone pays k squared fares. At the far bank the payout blooms as one lotus per trail, not per passenger, so n clones pay fourteen n receipts plus squared fares yet split one bloom while one honest agent sings once and keeps the flower.
